cls: Prostaglandin E1 - vasodilator / ductus arteriosus patency agent
quick: Erectile dysfunction (intracavernosal): individualized, e.g. 2.5-60 mcg per dose; neonatal PDA is the FDA-labeled IV use
Not applicable - given by IV infusion (neonate) or intracavernosal/intraurethral (ED)
Not applicable to neonatal use; ED indication is for men
No specific renal dose adjustment defined for neonatal infusion
No specific hepatic dose adjustment defined
Not relevant to the parenteral neonatal indication
Respiratory status (apnea), arterial pressure, pO2/pH, heart rate, body temperature
summary: Alprostadil is prostaglandin E1, a potent vasodilator and smooth-muscle relaxant. Its FDA-labeled intravenous use is palliative maintenance of ductus arteriosus patency in neonates with ductal-dependent congenital heart defects until surgery. It carries a boxed warning for apnea (about 10-12% of treated neonates), so it must be given where ventilatory support is immediately available. Alprostadil is also used (intracavernosal or intraurethral) for erectile dysfunction.
indications: Temporary maintenance of ductus arteriosus patency in neonates with ductal-dependent congenital heart defects (e.g. pulmonary atresia, tricuspid atresia, tetralogy of Fallot, transposition of the great vessels, coarctation, interrupted aortic arch) until corrective or palliative surgery
Treatment of erectile dysfunction (intracavernosal injection or intraurethral formulations)

dosage.d: Begin IV infusion at 0.05-0.1 mcg/kg/min; recommended starting dose 0.1 mcg/kg/min
dosage.n: After response, reduce to lowest effective rate (e.g. down to 0.01 mcg/kg/min)

dosage.d: Titrate down to 0.05, 0.025, then 0.01 mcg/kg/min to maintain response
dosage.n: Use lowest dose that maintains effect

dosage.d: Individualized, typically 2.5-60 mcg per injection titrated to response (Caverject/Edex)
dosage.t: As needed, max per product labeling
dosage.n: Not the FDA neonatal labeled use; per ED product label

admin: Neonatal: must be diluted before administration and given by continuous IV infusion into a large vein or umbilical artery catheter at the ductal opening
Administer only by trained personnel in a pediatric intensive care setting with ventilatory assistance immediately available
Infuse for the shortest time and lowest dose that achieves the desired effect
Erectile dysfunction: inject into the corpus cavernosum or use intraurethral system exactly as directed
moa: Alprostadil (prostaglandin E1) relaxes vascular and ductal smooth muscle. In neonates it acts directly on the smooth muscle of the ductus arteriosus to maintain or reopen patency, preserving systemic or pulmonary blood flow in ductal-dependent lesions. In the corpus cavernosum it increases cyclic AMP, relaxing trabecular smooth muscle and dilating cavernosal arteries to produce erection.

absolute: For the neonatal IV indication: none stated in labeling
ED use: conditions predisposing to priapism (sickle cell, multiple myeloma, leukemia), anatomic penile deformity, penile implants
relative: Neonates with respiratory distress syndrome (distinguish from cyanotic heart disease)
monitor: Arterial blood pressure and heart rate
Arterial pO2, pH, and oxygen saturation

preg: The intravenous neonatal indication does not involve maternal use; the erectile dysfunction indication is for men. Pregnancy considerations are not applicable.
lact: Not applicable to the indicated populations (neonates and men).
renal: No specific renal dose adjustment is defined for the neonatal infusion; titrate to clinical and physiologic response.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dose adjustment is defined; titrate to response.

moderate: Anticoagulants / antiplatelet agents (increased bleeding risk, especially with intracavernosal injection)
Other vasodilators / antihypertensives (additive hypotension with systemic exposure)
interactions.alcohol: Not relevant to the neonatal indication
interactions.diagnostics: May transiently affect arterial pO2 and acid-base parameters being monitored

serious: Gastric outlet obstruction from antral hyperplasia (prolonged use >120 h)

monitoring: Continuous respiratory monitoring (apnea, especially first hour and in infants <2 kg)
Arterial pressure (umbilical artery, auscultation, or Doppler)
Arterial blood gases (pO2, pH) and oxygen saturation
For prolonged infusion (>120 h): monitor for antral hyperplasia/gastric outlet obstruction and cortical hyperostosis
counsel: Neonatal therapy is given in intensive care; parents should understand it is a temporary measure before surgery
Apnea (pauses in breathing) is the most common serious effect and is watched for closely
For erectile dysfunction self-injection, follow injection technique exactly and rotate sites
Seek emergency care for an erection lasting more than 4 hours (ED use)
Report any bleeding, swelling, or pain at injection site
pk: Ductal relaxation often within minutes to a few hours of starting the infusion
Rapid; effect titrated to physiologic response
Very short - largely metabolized in a single pass through the lungs (about 70-80%)
Brief - requires continuous infusion to maintain effect
Refrigerate ampules at 2-8 C; dilute immediately before use and discard unused diluted solution
pearls: Boxed warning: apnea occurs in about 10-12% of treated neonates, usually within the first hour - ensure ventilatory support is immediately available
Almost completely metabolized on first pass through the lungs, hence the need for continuous infusion
Prolonged infusion (>120 h) risks antral hyperplasia/gastric outlet obstruction and cortical hyperostosis
Used both to maintain a ductal-dependent circulation (neonates) and for erectile dysfunction (men)
Best oxygenation response in neonates with the lowest pretreatment pO2
missed: Alprostadil is given as a continuous controlled infusion (neonates) or as needed before sexual activity (erectile dysfunction), so the concept of a missed scheduled dose does not apply. Maintain the infusion as ordered; do not interrupt without medical direction.
overdose: Overdose may manifest as apnea, bradycardia, flushing, hypotension, and pyrexia. If apnea or bradycardia occurs, stop the infusion and give appropriate supportive/resuscitative measures; for hypotension or flushing, reduce the infusion rate. Restart at a lower rate once stable.
